CodeWiki v0.5.1 makes architecture diagrams carry meaning. Color now shows which part of the system a component belongs to, each box names the code behind it, and figures get numbered captions. Pages can add note boxes, and hand-drawn SVG figures cover drawings Mermaid cannot express. Diagrams also gain zoom and pan.

## Highlights

- **Semantic groups.** Declare `groups` in `wiki.config.yaml`, each with a palette color (blue, green, violet, amber, red, teal, pink or slate) and an optional per-language label. Set `group:` on a page; child pages inherit it. Linked diagram nodes, their outgoing arrows (including arrowheads), single-group subgraphs, page headings and component cards then share the group's color, and every diagram gets a legend. `diagram_groups` assigns a group to nodes without a page. Every color has a light and a dark variant, and all pass 4.5:1 text contrast.
- **Code labels on diagram nodes.** A linked flowchart node shows the code behind it as a second line:
  - a section shows its first tagged declaration, such as `build.py · run()`;
  - a page shows its first owned file, such as `config.py +2`.

  The line comes from source tags, so it moves with the code. Turn it off with `diagram_code_labels: false`.
- **Captions and note boxes.** A `Figure:` paragraph after a diagram becomes a numbered caption. GitHub alert syntax (`> [!NOTE]`, `TIP`, `IMPORTANT`, `WARNING`, `CAUTION`) renders as a colored note box.
- **Hand-drawn SVG figures.** A relative `![alt](figures/x.svg)` on its own line is embedded in the page. The figure follows the theme, dark mode and group colors.
  - Inside the SVG, `data-group` sets group colors and `<a data-link="page.section">` creates a checked wiki link.
  - Strict builds reject missing or unsafe files, undeclared groups and broken links.
  - Editing a figure marks its page for review.
  - The `wiki-author` skill ships the drawing rules in `references/figures.md`.
- **Diagram zoom and pan.**
  - Zoom from 25% to 800% with buttons or the mouse wheel; the wheel zooms around the pointer. **Fit** resets the view.
  - Pan by dragging, including with touch. Dragging a linked node does not open it.
  - Keyboard: +/− to zoom, arrow keys to pan, 0 to fit.
  - The view is kept when the diagram is expanded or closed.
- **Agent and CLI output.** `query doc` and `index.json` now include page groups and SVG figures.

## Behavior changes to check when upgrading

- Linked flowchart nodes now show a second code line by default.
- A relative `.svg` image on a line of its own is now embedded and validated instead of shown as an `<img>`. Remote and absolute image URLs are unchanged.
- Two quotes separated by a blank line now render separately, as on GitHub. Before, they were merged into one.
- Mermaid, figure and alert syntax inside a longer code fence now stays literal code. Before, a nested ```` ```mermaid ```` block rendered as a diagram.
- Indexes built with 0.5.0 report as stale after the upgrade. Run `codewiki build --strict` once.

## Installation

Requires Python 3.10 or newer. Download the wheel below, then run:

```sh
python -m pip install ./codewiki_framework-0.5.1-py3-none-any.whl
```

For an existing initialized project, run `codewiki update --installed` after installing the wheel, then `codewiki build --strict`. This adds `skills/wiki-author/references/figures.md` and updates `skills/wiki-author/SKILL.md`. It does not refresh the Claude Code copies in `.claude/skills/`; copy the `wiki-author/` folder there yourself, including `references/`.

## Artifacts and validation

- Python wheel and source distribution, with SHA-256 checksums in `SHA256SUMS`.
- Built from main commit `{{commit}}` by the release workflow, which also:
  - ran the test suite on Python 3.10 and 3.13;
  - built the self-wiki with `--strict`;
  - installed the wheel in a fresh environment, ran `pip check`, initialized a project with Claude integration, built it with `--strict`, and ran a query.
- Checked before tagging, on Linux:
  - 119 tests passed on Python 3.10 and 3.13.
  - The Playwright diagram check passed: group colors, legend, captions, code labels, SVG figures, zoom, links, dialog, keyboard, mobile layout, localization and touch.
  - A project initialized with the v0.5.0 wheel upgraded with `codewiki update --installed`: 0 conflicts, then a strict build.
- The self-wiki still reports 4 pages pending documentation review: `user-manual`, `manual-maintaining`, `manual-review` and `test-languages`. The release did not acknowledge them.
